summary: A Waybar module that shows the current outdoor temperature for a saved latitude and longitude, fetched from the free Open-Meteo forecast API every 10 minutes, and opens the Open-Meteo page for that location when clicked.
targetUsers: Waybar users on Linux who want the current outdoor temperature in their status bar
Users who know their latitude and longitude and prefer a lightweight, no-account weather readout
goals: Show the current outdoor temperature as a Waybar module label for a saved latitude and longitude
Refresh the temperature from Open-Meteo every 10 minutes
Let the user save latitude and longitude with a command
Open the Open-Meteo page for the saved location in the browser when the module is clicked
nonGoals: Providing forecasts, hourly series, precipitation, wind, or any reading other than the current temperature
Geocoding a place name into coordinates
Detecting or enforcing that a reading is valid only for one calendar day
Storing a history of past temperatures

features.name: Show current temperature
features.userOutcome: The user sees the current outdoor temperature for the saved location in the Waybar module.
features.trigger: The Waybar module command re-reads the cached label, and the service loop refreshes the reading every 10 minutes.
features.behavior: The module command with no action or --once never fetches; it re-reads the cached label and renders it with the module label template. The --service loop and --action refresh call fetch_output, which requests the Open-Meteo forecast endpoint with the saved Latitude and Longitude, reads the current temperature from the documented response path, formats it with 1 decimal and the unit °C, and writes the cache label atomically. The reading is the first element of any list-valued response; a null, missing, or empty value is a failed fetch. The label class is normal. The user sets each coordinate with --set Latitude=VALUE and --set Longitude=VALUE, one command per field, and --action refresh applies the saved values immediately.
features.failureOutcome: When the fetch fails, the cache keeps the last good label text with class stale, and the module output rendered from that cache is that text with STALE_SUFFIX appended and class stale; no stored record changes. When no reading was ever stored, the label is --.
acceptanceSignals: With saved Latitude 52.52 and Longitude 13.41 and a successful fetch returning current.temperature_2m 21.34, the cache label text is 21.3 °C and the module output is 21.3 °C with class normal.
After a failed refresh, the module output is the last good label text with STALE_SUFFIX appended and class stale.
With no stored reading, the module output label is --.
The refresh pass returns runsEverySeconds 600 for this feature.

features.name: Open location page
features.userOutcome: The user reaches the Open-Meteo page for the saved location in the browser.
features.trigger: The user clicks the Waybar module.
features.behavior: On click, the feature reads the stored Latest temperature record and the saved Latitude and Longitude, builds the Open-Meteo page address with the saved coordinates percent-encoded, and opens it in the default browser. With no stored record it sends nothing and exits non-zero. A failed click shows no JSON and makes the command exit non-zero.
features.failureOutcome: With no stored record the click sends nothing and exits non-zero; a failed click shows no JSON and exits non-zero.
acceptanceSignals: With a stored Latest temperature record and saved Latitude 52.52 and Longitude 13.41, a click requests the browser open the Open-Meteo page address containing the percent-encoded coordinates.
With no stored Latest temperature record, a click sends nothing and the command exits non-zero.

dataObjects.name: Location settings
dataObjects.purpose: The saved latitude and longitude the temperature fetch and the location page use.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: Kept until the user overwrites a coordinate with --set or by editing config.json.

dataObjects.name: Latest temperature
dataObjects.purpose: The most recent successfully fetched current outdoor temperature for the saved location.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: Only the latest reading is kept; each successful refresh replaces the single stored row.

externalServices.name: Open-Meteo forecast
externalServices.purpose: Provides the current outdoor temperature for the saved latitude and longitude.

qualityRequirements: The module label shows the temperature with exactly 1 decimal and the unit °C, for example 21.3 °C.
The cache label is written atomically per record after each successful fetch.
The module command with no action or --once performs no network request.
productConstraints: The temperature source is the free Open-Meteo forecast API and requires no account or API key.
Coordinates are saved one field per command with --set Latitude=VALUE and --set Longitude=VALUE.
The refresh interval is fixed at 10 minutes.
